name: optional-traversal
intent: Make a partial or plural focus of a data structure a first-class, composable accessor, so that reading and updating it stays total and structure-preserving when the nested field is absent or when there are several of them.
problem: Every call site that reads or updates a nested field must decide what to do when the field may be missing (nothing to read, nothing to update) or when the addressed collection has zero, one or many elements; that conditional logic is duplicated, drifts between the read path and the write path, and has to be rewritten whenever the shape of the data changes.
context: Value-semantic or immutable domain data whose nested fields are optional and whose nested collections are updated through the same path from several places; at home in languages that provide an absence value plus a collection pipeline, or an optics library, and in situations where the path itself is worth keeping as a value instead of re-deriving it per call site.
benefits: Absence stops being a per-call-site problem: the accessor defines what a missing target means, so readers and writers no longer repeat guards.
One description covers zero, one or many targets, so a path whose cardinality changes (a field becomes a list, a list shrinks to at most one entry) does not force call sites to change shape.
Accessors compose: an optional focus composed with a lens, a prism or another traversal yields another accessor, so deep paths are assembled from small reusable pieces and can be shared as constants.
Structure-preserving updates avoid hand-written copy chains: the update function touches only the focused elements, and siblings, ordering and container shape are preserved by construction.
One traversal serves both reading and writing: the same path can collect or summarise targets (fold) or apply an effect to each of them, so the read and write views of the path cannot drift apart.
Optionality becomes visible in the type or the API: callers see that the focus may be absent or plural instead of discovering it as a runtime null dereference or an empty collection.
tradeoffs: The machinery must be learned, imported and threaded through types; for a single call site a local null check or a plain map is cheaper and clearer.
Composed traversal pipelines allocate intermediate collections, streams or closures and call a function per target; a hand-written loop with an early exit is faster on hot paths.
A traversal to an empty or wrong path silently does nothing; fallback or first-of combinators hide the mistake further unless tests assert how many targets matched.
Hand-written optics can violate the traversal laws - overlapping targets visited twice, or filters that break fusion - and composition then misbehaves in ways that are hard to localise.

On mutable or aliased data the structure-preservation promise breaks: the same node can be visited twice, and in C-style pointer traversal a NULL or dangling pointer is undefined behaviour rather than a skipped target.
Total skipping loses information: a traversal cannot always tell the caller whether the target was absent or present but filtered out, so that distinction must be modelled explicitly when it matters.

participants.responsibility: The whole value being addressed: a record, collection or tree whose nested parts are the focus of the accessor.
The first-class path that may focus zero or one target (Optional, affine traversal) or zero to many targets (Traversal), independent of the operation applied through it.
The element or elements the accessor addresses; absent values and empty structures legitimately produce no focus, and the operation then becomes an identity no-op.
The per-target operation applied through the accessor; it sees only the focused value, never the surrounding structure.
How per-target results are reassembled - first error, all errors, collected list - typically supplied by the applicative or monad used for the effect.
What happens at zero targets (no-op, default value or failure) and whether the caller can distinguish absent from filtered out.

use_cases: Optional configuration or feature-flag sections where whole blocks may be absent and the default belongs with the accessor rather than at every read site.
Nested request or DTO shapes where an intermediate object may be missing and the same path is used both to read a value and to patch it.
Bulk updates over a collection-valued field - repricing order lines, normalising tags, applying a discount - while keeping the collection and its order intact.
Domain validation: traverse all present fields, skip the optional ones, and accumulate per-field errors by running the traversal with an error-accumulating applicative.
Derived-value maintenance: recalculate every present element or clear a flag across a subtree through one composable path.
JSON- or document-shaped data where a path expression may match zero, one or many nodes and the caller wants one operation that handles all three cardinalities.
In Haskell's lens package, compose a Traversal with lenses to validate or normalize every matching field, using traverseOf or mapMOf for updates and effects.
In Scala Monocle, compose Optional and Traversal optics to update a possibly present nested value or all elements of a container, with getOption or getAll and law tests.
In Kotlin Arrow Optics, use Optional for a possibly absent nested focus and Traversal/Every to modify all elements in immutable data, composing optics through nested structures.
avoid_when: The field is guaranteed present: a direct property access or a lens is simpler, and modelled optionality then misleads readers.
You need to stop at the first matching target: a find/first or a short-circuiting search says that directly, while a traversal visits everything.
The structure is mutable, singly owned and performance-critical: a plain loop or in-place mutation is simpler and avoids intermediate allocations.
The language idiom already covers the single case and the path is not reused - optional chaining plus a default, or Optional.map - where an optics dependency would add cost without reuse.
Absence is an error rather than a legitimate case: fail-fast validation at the boundary keeps that distinction, which total skipping erases.
anti_patterns: Reaching for a traversal where a plain filter/map or a single optional-chaining expression already expresses the intent: machinery without reuse.
Treating a traversal like a lens - assuming exactly one target and unwrapping it - so an absent focus crashes or only the first element is updated.
Combining non-disjoint traversals that visit the same target twice, producing double updates and law violations.
Swallowing the zero-target case without asserting it, so a wrong path looks like a successful no-op.
Modelling every absent field as a traversal although the difference between absent and present-with-value is domain-relevant and gets lost.
design_principles: Explicit totality: absence is a value handled by the accessor, not an exception or a null check repeated at every site.
Separate the path from the operation: an accessor says where to look, an update function says what to do there.
Composition over special cases: partial, plural and single focuses compose, so one mechanism covers all cardinalities.
Structure preservation: updates change the focused elements and nothing else; shape and ordering are invariants.
Informative types: the possibility of absence or plurality belongs in the accessor's type or documented contract, not in a comment.
best_practices: Keep composed traversals as reusable values (constants or module-level accessors) and apply them from every call site instead of rebuilding the path.
Define zero-target behaviour explicitly and test it: an empty traversal must be an identity no-op or a documented default, never an accident.
Prefer the language's own idiom for a single, non-reused path; adopt an optics library only when paths are composed or shared.
Assert the number of matched targets in tests, because silent skipping and first-of fallbacks hide wrong paths.
Keep combined targets disjoint, and document target semantics when overlap is possible.
For immutable updates, verify structure preservation - untouched siblings, element order and container shape unchanged - not just the focused values.
sources: Pickering, Gibbons & Wu, Profunctor Optics: Modular Data Accessors, The Art, Science, and Engineering of Programming 1(2) (2017) - optics taxonomy: lenses, prisms and traversals and their composition.

Kmett et al., lens - Control.Lens.Traversal (Hackage, functional-catalog lexicon): the Traversal optic as a generalization of Data.Traversable's traverse, usable as Fold, Setter and composed pipeline.
